derivation: Measured via the calibration procedure in Task 5's brief (200 trials, torch.manual_seed(0), 2000-sample synthetic signals): known-correct cases pair two independent randn(2000) sources with 5%-noise, cross-scaled copies of each other (0.8x and 1.2x) so exactly one assignment is right; ambiguous cases pair a single randn(2000) source with two near-identical 1%-noise copies of itself so no assignment is right. best_score - second_best_score over sorted(_assignment_scores(...)): known-correct p05/p50 = 1.93 / 2.00 (min 1.89, max 2.14); ambiguous p50/p95 = 2.3e-6 / 6.1e-6 (max 9.3e-6). The two distributions are separated by more than five orders of magnitude on this synthetic construction, which validates that the scale-invariant correlation metric itself discriminates a real permutation swap from a genuine tie -- that is what the test suite in source_separation_test.py checks. It does NOT constitute a measurement of real unasdiff output: both categories here are independent-Gaussian constructions, not the actual overlap-region statistics of two consecutive 4 s diffusion-sampled windows, which this environment cannot produce (no GPU, no built venv, no separated audio to measure against). Per CLAUDE.md's standing rule against literals that were never fitted, min_assignment_margin is deliberately omitted rather than interpolated between these synthetic bounds -- see the note field. Until a threshold is fitted against real unasdiff windows, senselab.audio.tasks.source_separation.unasdiff.separate_with_unasdiff reports every window boundary's margin in metadata['unasdiff_alignment_margins'] instead of gating on one.
note: min_assignment_margin is intentionally absent from this profile -- do not add a placeholder value. See derivation.
first_real_measurements: VOID -- do not calibrate against these. Measured on an H100 (2026-08-10, job 20080852) on a 4.92 s clip, one window boundary each: speech_speech 0.0109, speech_sound 0.0579. They were read at the time as real margins falling between the two synthetic regimes. They were not: that clip is exactly the case where _window_starts appends a final window flush against the end of the signal, overlapping its predecessor by 49280 samples rather than the regular 32000, and the alignment step was slicing a fixed overlap_samples off each side. The two compared regions were therefore offset by 17280 samples, and because the score is a dot product after normalisation, content shared at different indices contributes nothing -- so every permutation scored ~0 and the margin measured the offset, not the separation. The numbers are an artifact of the defect, reproduced deterministically as 0.027 by source_separation_test.py::test_irregular_final_window_aligns_on_its_true_shared_region against the ~2.0 the same input yields once the shared region is derived per window pair. No real-hardware margin has been measured since the fix; the calibration this field was meant to start still needs one.
